title: Open Muse and sort a tiny list
summary: Find Meta’s helper. Give it a job you can check before you ask it for bigger things.
where: Use muse.ai in a browser or the official Muse app from Meta. On iPad, check the App Store age and device rules with an adult. You can do the sorting exercise on paper.

actions.title: Find Muse
actions.do: Enter muse.ai in the address box. Open the page from Meta. Use its app link if you want the app.
actions.see: The page or app says Muse and identifies Meta.
actions.stuck: If a search shows another app called Muse, return to the official link.

actions.title: Open the message box
actions.do: Sign in with an account that can use Muse. Open Chat. Find the box labeled Message.
actions.see: There is a place to type and a button to send.
actions.stuck: If you cannot sign in, write the next request on paper and do it yourself.

actions.title: Sort three words
actions.do: Ask: Put these in ABC order. Blue, Gold, Aqua. Compare the first letter of each word.
actions.see: Aqua comes first, Blue second and Gold last.
actions.stuck: If it leaves a word out, count the words in your request and its reply.

actions.title: Change the list
actions.do: Ask it to add Green and sort again. Compare Gold with Green one letter at a time.
actions.see: The four words are Aqua, Blue, Gold, Green.
actions.stuck: The second letter breaks the tie between the two G words.

roles: Put headings for a meeting in ABC order.
Check list sorting in a game.
sources: Apple · Muse from Meta, compatibility and age rating
Meta · download Muse for your device
Meta · the launch of Muse in Australia

title: Plan a trip backward from the start time
summary: Can you reach a ferry before boarding closes? Check Muse’s plan with a clock.
where: Open Chat in Muse. A side chat is a place to keep just one task and its replies together.

actions.title: Name a side chat
actions.do: Open the chat menu. Use its pencil or new-chat control to start a side chat for Ferry plan.
actions.see: Your new chat has its own place in the list.
actions.stuck: If you opened the main chat, open the menu again and look for side chats.

actions.title: Set three times
actions.do: Type: The ferry leaves at 10:30. Boarding closes 20 minutes before that. The walk takes 15 minutes. When must I leave?
actions.see: Boarding closes at 10:10. Leaving at 9:55 gets you there then.
actions.stuck: Count back on a clock. Take off 20 minutes, then 15.

actions.title: Add a cushion
actions.do: Ask to reach the pier 10 minutes before boarding closes. Keep the sailing time and walk length the same.
actions.see: Arrive at 10:00. Leave at 9:45.
actions.stuck: If the sailing time changes, repeat the three original facts and name only the new cushion.

actions.title: Find your plan again
actions.do: Ask for three lines labeled Leave, Arrive and Boarding closes. Close and reopen the side chat.
actions.see: The times still read 9:45, 10:00 and 10:10.
actions.stuck: If you find an older plan, look for the follow-up that added ten minutes.

roles: Plan when to start a report.
Work back from a meeting time.
Check the countdown in a timer app.

title: See what a helper can read or change
summary: Connecting another app is like handing over a key. Read what the key opens.
where: Open Muse Settings. This practice uses a made-up event. You can leave your calendar disconnected.

actions.title: Look at the choices
actions.do: Open Connectors. Pick a calendar option to read its description. Stop before connecting any account.
actions.see: The screen tells you which service Muse is asking to use.
actions.stuck: If you reach a sign-in screen, go back. You can practice with the sample.

actions.title: Compare two jobs
actions.do: Imagine two jobs: list tomorrow’s events and add a new event. Which one needs permission to change a calendar?
actions.see: Listing needs permission to read. Adding needs permission to write.
actions.stuck: Read the verbs on the screen. Look for view, create or change.

actions.title: Draft with a note
actions.do: In Chat type: Practice starts June 8 at 1 p.m. and ends at 1:30. Draft a reminder. Show the words here.
actions.see: The reminder uses the two times. It takes no live calendar to write it.
actions.stuck: If Muse offers to create an event, ask it to show you just the text.

actions.title: Find the controls
actions.do: Return to Settings and open Permissions. Look for where you could review access or an action before it happens.
actions.see: You know where to look before giving a real tool a job.
actions.stuck: If your account shows other choices, read its description before choosing one.

roles: Use sample mail rows to practice reading.
Look at an invite before adding it to a calendar.
Plan access for an app that only reads scores.
sources: Meta · connecting or disconnecting a service

title: Set one reminder and find it again
summary: Make a short reminder you can test without waiting all day.
where: Open Muse Chat. Pick a time about ten minutes ahead. Use your device’s time zone.

actions.title: Name one reminder
actions.do: Ask: Remind me once today at my chosen time to check the packing list. Replace the time in that sentence with your actual time.
actions.see: Muse should show a reminder with the words packing list.
actions.stuck: If you meant once, check that it does not say every day.

actions.title: Read the schedule
actions.do: Tap the assistant icon. Choose Upcoming and open your reminder. Read the date, time and repeat setting.
actions.see: They match your request.
actions.stuck: If the hour is off, check the time zone and fix the practice reminder.

actions.title: Watch for the result
actions.do: After the time has passed, open the chat again. Look for the reminder there.
actions.see: The message mentions the packing list.
actions.stuck: If there was no device alert, look in the chat before making a second reminder.

actions.title: Check what is left
actions.do: Look in Upcoming once more. If your practice item is set to repeat, open it and cancel just that item.
actions.see: A one-time reminder has no next run after delivery.
actions.stuck: Use the item’s name and time to avoid changing a different reminder.

roles: Remind yourself to check a sample report.
Test a reminder feature in your own app.

title: Find and fix a file Muse made
summary: A chat reply can describe a file. Open the file itself to see what was saved.
where: Open Muse Chat. You will give it three made-up packing items. Library is where Muse keeps finished files.

actions.title: Ask for a file
actions.do: Ask for a plain-text file called Game Kit with one item per line: cards, pencils, timer.
actions.see: Look for a file card you can open.
actions.stuck: If all you get is a message, ask Muse to create the actual text file.

actions.title: Open the saved copy
actions.do: Choose Library. Find Game Kit and open it. Count its lines.
actions.see: There are three items. Timer is last.
actions.stuck: If you see several versions, check the file name and the newest result.

actions.title: Change one item
actions.do: Ask to replace timer with clock in Game Kit. Keep the other two lines in order.
actions.see: Only the last line should change.
actions.stuck: If it makes a second file, find out which one holds your new list.

actions.title: Test the saved file
actions.do: Close the preview. Open the newest Game Kit from Library and read it again.
actions.see: It says cards, pencils, clock. That proves the edit was saved.
actions.stuck: If it still says timer, point Muse to the exact file you checked.

roles: Update a shared supply list for practice.
Find the file your app created.

title: Change one thing in a picture
summary: Give Muse a simple picture request. See whether it keeps the rest when you ask for one edit.
where: Open Muse Chat. You can draw the same comparison on paper if your account cannot make images.

actions.title: Ask for a simple picture
actions.do: Type: Make a square picture of one red mug with one blue star on a cream table.
actions.see: You have four things to check: shape, mug count, color and star.
actions.stuck: If you see two mugs, request one mug before changing anything else.

actions.title: Inspect it
actions.do: Open the picture. Check the star and the edge of the frame first. Then check the mug.
actions.see: The frame is square and the mug has just one blue star.
actions.stuck: Write your four checks on paper if one is easy to miss.

actions.title: Ask for one edit
actions.do: Say: Change only the mug from red to green. Keep the star, table and frame the same.
actions.see: The new mug is green. The star stays blue.
actions.stuck: If the star changes too, use the earlier version and name both colors again.

actions.title: Compare the copies
actions.do: Open both versions and look at them at a small size. Pick the one that meets the request.
actions.see: You can explain your choice using visible details.
actions.stuck: If they look alike in the chat list, open each picture before choosing.

roles: Make simple art for a mail help note.
Illustrate one picture in a training guide.
Try two versions of an app icon.
